```{r}
# ---- Bulk CI composition, two sourced options -------------------------
# Kept as two SEPARATELY NAMED vectors on purpose: reassigning the same
# name twice (as this file used to do) means the second definition
# silently wins and the first becomes unreachable dead code - the same
# stale-duplicate-definition pattern flagged elsewhere in this project.
# Units mg/g. Table 6 (b_raw, main .Rmd) is EITHER of these times 1.4683
# +/- 0.0038 (n=14, see ANHYDROUS_TO_BULK): Table 6 therefore carries NO
# independent information. Perturb THESE vectors, never Table 6.

# Alexander (2019) GCA 254:277-309, Table 1, column "CI".
# O is BACK-CALCULATED from Table 6 (293.2/1.4683) because Table 1 reports
# oxygen split into anhydrous (Oan) and excess (Oex) rather than as a
# single value - this O is not an independent bulk measurement.
b_bulk_CI_AlexanderT1 <- c(Mg = 95.4,  Al = 8.4,   Si = 107.0, Ca = 9.11,
               Ti = 0.440, Cr = 2.62,  Mn = 1.92,  K  = 0.546,
               Na = 4.96,  P  = 0.985, S  = 53.5,  Fe = 185.0,
               Ni = 10.6,  Co = 0.519, O  = 293.2 / 1.4683)

# Lodders et al. (2025) Table 4, column "CI".
# 2026-09-14: moved to the main .Rmd (it is now also the source for the
# primary point-estimate fit, b_CI_Lodders) so there is one copy, not
# two -- a second copy here previously duplicated it, the same
# stale-duplicate-definition pattern this file's own header warns about.
# `b_bulk_CI_LoddersT4` is defined in Primordial_CI_chondrite_mineralogy.Rmd,
# which must be sourced/run before this file. O here (465.7) is Lodders'
# TOTAL bulk-CI oxygen (hydrous) -- it is used below ONLY as the
# denominator for sigma_rel_Lodders, never as a fit target; recompute_O()
# (also now defined in the main .Rmd) replaces it before any fit runs.

# ACTIVE choice for the Monte Carlo below.
b_bulk_CI <- b_bulk_CI_LoddersT4


# ---- Relative uncertainties --------------------------------------------
# Two sourced options, same reasoning as above: separate names, one
# ACTIVE choice, so the discarded option stays legible instead of being
# silently overwritten.

# DECLARED ASSUMPTION, not measurement (pairs with b_bulk_CI_AlexanderT1).
# Table 1 gives no uncertainties. The one element with a real spread is S:
# Alexander et al. (2021) Table 4 lists five independent CI determinations
# (5.20, 5.24, 5.35, 5.40, 6.07 wt%) -> 6.5% RSD. In the absence of
# anything better, 5% is applied to majors and 10% to minors, with S at
# its measured 6.5%. REPLACE with Palme et al. (2014) uncertainties if you
# can get them (RECONSTRUCTION_STATUS.md open item #1).
sigma_rel_assumed <- c(Mg = 0.05, Al = 0.05, Si = 0.05, Ca = 0.05, Ti = 0.10,
               Cr = 0.05, Mn = 0.05, K  = 0.10, Na = 0.05, P  = 0.10,
               S  = 0.065, Fe = 0.05, Ni = 0.05, Co = 0.10, O = 0.0)

# [Bug 1] Lodders et al. (2025) Table 4 1-sigma column. These are ABSOLUTE
# uncertainties in mg/g (matching b_bulk_CI_LoddersT4's units), NOT
# fractions. A prior run assigned this vector directly into `sigma_rel`,
# which mc_fit()/mc_fit2() use as a lognormal `sd` - i.e. a value that
# must be a FRACTION. That produced nonsensical draws (NNLS hitting
# maxit, phases collapsing to zero). Fix: keep the absolute values
# separate and divide by the composition they belong to.
sigma_abs_Lodders  <- c(Mg = 3.0, Al = 0.48, Si = 4.00, Ca = 0.544, Ti = 0.03,
               Cr = 0.116, Mn = 0.153, K  = 0.041, Na = 0.512, P  = 0.089,
               S  = 4.6, Fe = 6.0, Ni = 0.3, Co = 0.026, O = 8.0)
sigma_rel_Lodders <- sigma_abs_Lodders / b_bulk_CI_LoddersT4

# ACTIVE choice for the Monte Carlo below.
sigma_rel <- sigma_rel_Lodders

# Sanity check (handoff requirement): fractions should read approximately
# Si ~3.8-4.0%, Mg ~3.1%, Fe ~3.2%, Al ~5.7%, Ca ~5.9-6.1%, S ~8.9-9.3%,
# Na ~10.3%, O ~1.7%. If any land far outside this, stop - do not proceed.
print(round(100 * sigma_rel_Lodders, 2))


# ---- Oxygen: always recomputed, never read from a table ---------------
# [Bug 2 fix] `recompute_O()` moved to the main .Rmd, 2026-09-14 (same
# reasoning as b_bulk_CI_LoddersT4 above: single source of truth, since
# the main file's own primary fit now needs it too). Derives O from
# cation oxidation states - all lithophiles oxidised, Fe/Ni/Co/P reduced
# - never from a table.


# ---- Monte Carlo, naive baseline: independent per-element errors ------
# Elements are treated as INDEPENDENT, which is conservative: real
# compilations share sources, so Mg and Si errors are likely correlated,
# and correlated errors would leave Mg/Si -- the quantity that decides Fo
# vs En -- better constrained than this assumes. Superseded by mc_fit2()
# below, which models the shared component explicitly. Kept as the
# "before" baseline for that comparison, not as a second independent
# result to report.
mc_fit <- function(n = 2000, phases, fit_elements,
                   bulk = b_bulk_CI, sigma = sigma_rel, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, n, length(phases),
                dimnames = list(NULL, phases))
  ratio <- numeric(n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    s  <- sigma[names(bulk)]
    bp <- bulk * exp(rnorm(length(bulk),
                           mean = -s^2/2,   # so E[bp] = bulk
                           sd   = s))
    bp <- recompute_O(bp)                   # [Bug 2 fix] never bulk["O"]
    tgt <- drop_TiCo(bp)                    # [Bug 4 fix] no *1.4683: any
    # constant scalar applied here cancels in drop_TiCo's final
    # renormalisation to 1000 mg/g (verified algebraically - see
    # RECONSTRUCTION_STATUS.md), so it was a no-op left over from an
    # earlier draft. Removed for clarity, not because it was wrong.
    f <- tryCatch(fit_scenario(phases, tgt, fit_elements),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(f)) next
    out[i, ] <- f$wt_pct
    ratio[i] <- f$wt_pct["Enstatite"] / f$wt_pct["Forsterite"]
  }
  # p_En_gt_Fo REMOVED, 2026-09-13 (RECONSTRUCTION_STATUS.md §2): a
  # P(En>Fo) figure is a coin-flip statement about a ~50/50 split and
  # adds no information beyond "uncertain" -- do not reintroduce it here.
  # `en_fo` (the raw ratio draws) is kept for anyone who wants to inspect
  # the distribution directly, but it is not printed as a probability.
  list(modes = out, en_fo = ratio,
       summary = t(apply(out, 2, quantile,
                         c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)),
       p_An_zero  = mean(out[, "Anorthite"] < 1e-6, na.rm = TRUE))
}

mc_R_naive <- mc_fit(phases = phases_R, fit_elements = elements_R)
print(round(mc_R_naive$summary, 3))
cat("P(anorthite vanishes) =", mc_R_naive$p_An_zero, "\n")
```

```{r}
# Scenario R Monte Carlo, validated approach. Two changes from mc_fit():
#  (1) Mg and Si errors are CORRELATED. CI compilations share samples and
#      calibrations, and ratios cancel the systematics that dominate
#      absolute abundances (Alexander T1 molar Mg/Si = 1.0303; Lodders
#      2003 = 1.0398, 0.9% apart). Independent errors overstate
#      sigma(Mg/Si) -- the ONLY quantity that decides Fo vs En.
#      Modelled as a shared multiplicative factor plus a small
#      element-specific residual.
#  (2) O is RECOMPUTED from the perturbed cations via recompute_O(),
#      never read from bulk["O"] (see [Bug 2] above).

mc_fit2 <- function(n = 2000, phases, fit_elements,
                    bulk = b_bulk_CI, sigma = sigma_rel,
                    sigma_shared = 0.04,   # common-mode, cancels in ratios
                    seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  el  <- setdiff(names(bulk), "O")
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, n, length(phases), dimnames = list(NULL, phases))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    # sigma_ind is the part that does NOT cancel in a ratio. Total
    # per-element sigma is sqrt(shared^2 + ind^2); set shared so the
    # residual reproduces your sourced sigma(Mg/Si).
    s_ind <- sqrt(pmax(sigma[el]^2 - sigma_shared^2, 1e-6))
    bp <- bulk[el] * exp(rnorm(1, -sigma_shared^2/2, sigma_shared)) *
                     exp(rnorm(length(el), -s_ind^2/2, s_ind))
    bp  <- recompute_O(c(bp, O = 0))        # [Bug 2] never a table value
    tgt <- drop_TiCo(bp)                    # [Bug 4] no *1.4683 (no-op)
    f <- tryCatch(fit_scenario(phases, tgt, fit_elements),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(f)) out[i, ] <- f$wt_pct
  }
  fo <- out[, "Forsterite"]; en <- out[, "Enstatite"]
  # p_En_gt_Fo REMOVED, 2026-09-13 (RECONSTRUCTION_STATUS.md §2, closing
  # note): do not reintroduce it. `fo_frac` is the reported summary of
  # the split -- report it with its interval, not as a P(En>Fo) figure.
  list(modes = out,
       summary = t(apply(out, 2, quantile, c(0.025,0.5,0.975), na.rm=TRUE)),
       # Fo and En are strongly ANTI-correlated: Fo+En is well
       # constrained while the split is not, so report the split.
       fo_frac = quantile(fo/(fo+en), c(0.025,0.5,0.975), na.rm = TRUE),
       fo_plus_en = quantile(fo+en, c(0.025,0.5,0.975), na.rm = TRUE))
}

mc_R <- mc_fit2(phases = phases_R, fit_elements = elements_R)
print(round(mc_R$summary, 3))
cat("Fo/(Fo+En), 2.5/50/97.5%:\n")
print(round(mc_R$fo_frac, 4))
```

```{r}
# 1. Are Fo and En anti-correlated in the MC? Expect about -0.95.
cat("cor(Fo, En) =",
    cor(mc_R$modes[, "Forsterite"], mc_R$modes[, "Enstatite"], use = "complete"),
    "\n")

# 2. Does the NNLS solution equal the closed form? Expect ~0 both.
norm_closed <- function(b) {           # b in mg/g, reservoir basis
  m <- b / AW[names(b)]
  Si_rem <- m["Si"] - 3*m["Na"] - 3*m["K"] - 2*m["Ca"] - 0.5*m["Mn"]
  Mg_rem <- m["Mg"] - m["Ca"] + 0.5*(m["Al"] - m["Na"] - m["K"]) - 0.5*m["Cr"]
  c(Fo = unname((Mg_rem - Si_rem) * 140.693),
    En = unname((2*Si_rem - Mg_rem) * 100.389),
    r  = unname(Mg_rem / Si_rem))
}
# 2026-09-14: fit_R now targets b_CI_Lodders, not b_CI (RECONSTRUCTION_
# STATUS.md S1, Lodders is primary) -- this check must validate against
# the SAME composition fit_R was actually fit to, or it compares two
# different targets and reports a spurious mismatch. Updated accordingly.
# norm_closed() is unaffected by the 2026-09-14 P/Schreibersite addition
# either way: P and Fe3P carry no Mg or Si, so Fo/En are untouched by it.
cat("closed form (Fo, En) - NNLS (Fo, En), mg/g:\n")
print(norm_closed(b_CI_Lodders)[c("Fo","En")] - c(fit_R$mg_g["Forsterite"], fit_R$mg_g["Enstatite"]))

# 2b. Closed-form crossover check (handoff verification task B). Mass
# crossover (Fo = En by mass) is at Mg_rem/Si_rem = 1.4164 -- solving
# 140.693*(r-1) = 100.389*(2-r) for r:
#   140.693 r - 140.693 = 200.778 - 100.389 r    (2*100.389 = 200.778)
#   241.082 r = 341.471                          (140.693 + 100.389)
#   r = 341.471 / 241.082 = 1.41642
crossover_r <- (2*100.389 + 140.693) / (140.693 + 100.389)
cat("Crossover r solved here:", round(crossover_r, 4),
    "| RECONSTRUCTION_STATUS.md claims 1.4164\n")

r_actual <- norm_closed(b_CI_Lodders)["r"]
cat("Actual r (b_CI_Lodders):", round(r_actual, 4),
    "| distance from crossover:",
    sprintf("%.2f%%\n", 100 * (r_actual - crossover_r) / crossover_r))
r_actual_Alexander <- norm_closed(b_CI)["r"]
cat("Actual r (b_CI, Alexander bracket):", round(r_actual_Alexander, 4),
    "| distance from crossover:",
    sprintf("%.2f%%\n", 100 * (r_actual_Alexander - crossover_r) / crossover_r))

# 3. Is the perturbed system still exactly solvable? Expect ~0.
#    If not, NNLS is distributing a misfit and that would decouple Fo/En.
cat("max |resid_pct| Scenario R fit:", max(abs(fit_R$residual$resid_pct)), "\n")
```
